body_markdown:
Ford is digging into its back catalog with a new paint option for the most popular cab-and-bed configuration of the 2027 F-150 pickup. The Custom Two-Tone Package slathers a horizontal stripe in Oxford White, Carbonized Gray, or Agate Black onto pickups as a factory ship-through order. The painted stripe stretches around the front of the truck from just below the beltline to just above the rockers and is backed by a 3-year, 36,000-mile warranty. The 2027 F-150 Custom Two-Tone Package has an MSRP of $12,545, which can be rolled into the lease or finance price.


Ford


The two-tone stripe option is available only on SuperCrew F-150s with the standard 5.5-foot bed and can be added to XLT and Lariat trims. Buyers must select the custom paint on the initial order; Ford won’t open the option to trucks that have already been sold. It will be available over top of 10 factory F-150 paint colors.


Some of our favorite trucks from the ‘60s, ‘70s, and ‘80s were offered with two-tone paint, and the F-150 certainly has the right lines to pull it off. The option, particularly in red and white, gives the truck a bit of an ‘80s throwback vibe without looking too retro. Perhaps we’re just used to seeing two-tone trucks, even though it has been several generations since they were a standard offering from Ram, Ford, and GM. For a long while, it seemed that two-tone was the norm until tastes shifted and the option disappeared in the ‘90s. Buyers who wanted a bit of that vintage style had to rely on the aftermarket, either via vinyl wrap or paint.

We’re always excited to see OEMs offering customers more choices, but the five-figure option is steep at around 20% of the entry cost of a Lariat SuperCrew. Ford has offered some pricey paint protection before, with factory-applied[wrap options on the Mustang since 2024](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2025-ford-mustang-convertible-matte-clear-film-option/) , but this custom two-tone is different and requires a lot more labor. That said, now that we’ve seen Ford dip a toe in the water, can we get some more graphics on pickups? Pretty please? Don’t let the Bronco have all the fun.


The Big Three offered two-tone and various stripe options for years. Here’s a sampling from vintage brochures. Which do you think did it best, and what stripe combos or two-tones ought to make a comeback on a current production pickup?
